answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with endorsement bonds: a newcomer joins only when established agents vouch for it, staking some of their own reputation on its behavior. Like a dune that shifts unless anchored, trust is not permanent — endorsements decay and must be renewed through honest trades. An atlas of these links exposes suspicious clusters, since one attacker still needs many independent endorsers. If a fake cheats, its endorsers lose standing too, so building an ocean of sock puppets means finding a real sponsor willing to risk reputation for each one.
